description.p: Stellarator collects training data from language models. Point it at a model server, give it a set of prompts, and it sends every prompt to the model, keeps the prompt with the model's thinking trace and its answer, and exports the result as a dataset for fine-tuning or preference training.

It works with any server that offers the OpenAI chat completions API: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio on your own hardware, or a hosted API such as OpenRouter. It does not train or serve models; it talks to the server you already have.

ul.li: Presets for OpenRouter, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp
Prompts from Hugging Face datasets, Markdown, text, CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL or Parquet files, or pasted text
Only the prompts are imported: answer columns and assistant turns are left out
Change the number of sequences in flight while a run is going, and see the effect on throughput
Retries with backoff, and a run that pauses itself after repeated failures
Thinking traces from reasoning_content, reasoning or inline think tags
Side-by-side review to mark chosen and rejected answers
Exports as chat messages, ShareGPT, Alpaca, prompt-completion, raw, DPO or KTO records, in JSONL, JSON, Parquet or CSV, or pushed to the Hugging Face Hub

description.p: Data stays on your computer. There is no account and no sign-in.

screenshot.caption: A run in progress: progress, throughput against seqs, and the sequences in flight
Importing prompts from a Hugging Face dataset, with the answer columns left out
Preference review: candidate answers side by side, with Choose and Reject
Export: pick a format and see the first record as it will be written

ul.li: The window is drawn with GTK 4 instead of a web page, and the server runs inside the app with no network port
Less memory: one process and no web view
Only one copy runs per data folder, and the window opens where you left it
Stopping an import that has just finished keeps the prompt set
Needs GTK 4.14 or later: Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or later
Users of 0.3 download this version by hand; their data is kept

description.p: Windows: the app opens its database again.

ul.li: A new design: Inter for text, Roboto Mono for data, neutral grays with a periwinkle accent, and cards set apart by tone
Detail screens open with a large title, chips for status, model, endpoint and prompt set, and the key facts as tiles
Frosted materials on the toolbar, menus, dialogs, sheets and the floating action bars
The run chart counts back from now, leaves out paused time, and shows the change in tokens per second after seqs change
A simpler mark and a new app icon
A floating sidebar and a toolbar at the top of each page
Frosted menus, dialogs and sheets that stay legible over anything behind them
Simple import mode: paste a Hugging Face link and the prompt column, split and first user turn are picked for you
Display math on its own line renders as display math

description.p: The first release of the desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux.
